why: The classic two-heaps pattern: a max-heap holds the smaller half and a min-heap the larger half, balanced to within one element, so the median is read from the heap tops after each add.
hints: Sorting after every add is O(n log n) per query. You only ever need the middle one or two values.
Split the values into a lower half (max-heap) and an upper half (min-heap); the median lives at their tops.
On add, push into the lower heap, move its top to the upper heap, then rebalance so lower has the same size or one more. Median = lower top, or the mean of both tops. O(log n) per add.
pitfalls: Python's heapq is a min-heap; store negatives for the max-heap.
Return floats: (1 + 5) / 2 = 3.0, and an odd count still returns e.g. 5.0.
Values can be negative; do not use integer division for the mean.
